strongest_case: V4 retains a coherent and deliberately narrow finite symbolic kernel. Under the natural inverse rendering of the descriptor-to-role bijection, the 96 alignments quotient to 48 graphs and six calibration classes of 16; each calibration-goal cell has four TOP pairs at count four; the full factorized RANDOM product preserves value 1/4; MOTIF_SCHEMA and ORACLE have direct value 1; tau is involutive and changes all registered graph and goal content; costs are 5, 8, 16, and 17; and the exact namespace-tagged deletion intervention has 36,864 bridge cases and 73,728 checks. V4 correctly removes substitution, binds one 1,476-byte successful report, makes failures nonzero with no success report, moves SK10 outside the runtime graph, permits only the preapproval governance chain, and preserves exact three-atom requested and eight-atom forbidden scope. This mathematics is non-headline symbolic conformance only: LOCAL is target-local information, not an atoms baseline, and neither MOTIF access, the golden, nor an audit is a learned-system, benchmark, model, promotion, or paper result. The exact proposal nevertheless requires REWORK before implementation ratification. The science reading correctly finds SK10's absent implementation binding and the scope reading correctly adds the incomplete external-audit visibility and successor-lineage defects. Those are not merely notes: the seven-key receipt cannot identify every frozen implementation byte, cannot prove a complete deterministic audit closure or reviewer freshness, and the matrix exposes outputs without the evidence inputs from which SK10 must derive them. The successor defect is also blocking but must be stated more carefully than the scope interpretation: v3 was a rework proposal, not a ratified active graph, so v4 fails under every plausible base rule—replacement of v3 omits v3's removals and has no declared replacement semantics; composition with hypothetical v3 collides on SKN01 and SKE01-SKE09 and retains renamed nodes and loop; standalone application leaves modify/retire targets and the prior active registry undefined. Two additional predecessor requirements remain unresolved: GRAPH never explicitly applies pi inverse or binds fixed vectors, and SK08 has no exact nonempty malformed-call registry or receipt count, so aggregate self-consistency cannot detect the wrong relabeling and zero negative failures can be vacuous. The ratification change-hash item is a material literal mismatch, not a provenance failure: architecture_intake transitively binds the exact change through consensus and paused state, but the ratification schema has no direct change_sha256 property for the visibility cell to expose. These defects must be dispositioned without weakening the terminal firewall or inferring authority.

The bound algebra yields 96 alignments, 48 graphs, six calibration classes of 16, four goal-conditioned TOP pairs at count four, values 1/4 for LOCAL and RANDOM_SOURCE and 1 for MOTIF_SCHEMA and ORACLE, an involutive content-changing tau, costs 5/8/16/17, 36,864 bridge cases, and 73,728 typed deletion checks. The report is one fixed terminal successful object and SK10 is external. These are specification facts pending implementation; they contain no renderer, life, target agent, DREAM/SLEEP, memory, model, tokenizer, LoRA, GPU, learned representation, fair baseline, promotion, benchmark, or scientific result. C04 correctly says LOCAL is target-local rather than atoms, and MOTIF reads the complete persistent graph rather than learning schema.

concerns.statement: V4 does not identify a predecessor state or replacement rule under which its add/modify/retire operations yield the claimed exact five-node, nine-edge, two-loop successor.
concerns.evidence: The scope interpretation is right that all five nodes, all nine edges, and both loops are marked add, while v3 used SKN01_AUTHORITY and SKE01-SKE09 and used differently named SKN02-SKN05 plus SKL01_EXACT_SYMBOLIC_KERNEL. Its claim registry was C01_instrument_eligibility through C08_phase_diagram_and_credit_boundary, not v4's new C01-C06 IDs. The nuance is that bound v3 consensus recommends rework and forbids implementation, so those v3 additions are not an active ratified base. That does not cure v4. If v4 replaces the unratified v3 proposal, no replacement semantics are declared and v4 omits v3's removals of the older N/E/L registry. If it composes after v3 hypothetically, duplicate SKN01/SKE identifiers collide and renamed nodes and SKL01 remain. If it applies standalone to the last ratified architecture, its modify/retire claim targets and intended removals are undefined. Structural validation checks only uniqueness inside v4 and cannot choose among these bases. The exact final active registry is therefore implementer-selected.

concerns.statement: SK10's seven-key receipt cannot bind every frozen implementation byte or establish a deterministic complete and fresh independent audit, so it does not repair bound v3 resolution R05.
concerns.evidence: Both interpretations correctly identify the root defect. The exact keys contain change_sha256 and reviewer_interpretation_sha256 but no implementation hash, per-file digest map, root manifest, audited tree or commit identity, diff-base identity, or deterministic relation between tracked_files and bytes. The subset predicates allow tracked_files and observed_imports to omit the actual implementation and dependency closure; the CLI sentence does not bind how entrypoints are discovered; static AST/import/string and repository-diff review has no exact root, inclusion/exclusion rules, symlink/generated-file policy, transitive dependency/option/hook/dormant-capability closure, forbidden-token or reachability algorithm, or complete changed-file equality. The referenced reviewer interpretation has no bound schema, path, required fields, reviewer identity, independence predicate, creation-after-freeze relation, or validation rule. Consequently passed=true and empty forbidden_matches can be produced over different or incomplete subjects, and the phrase all hashes match is unsatisfiable for an implementation hash that the object cannot carry. Keeping SK10 external is correct, but external evidence still needs an exact source-bound schema and procedure.

concerns.statement: The mechanically complete 120-by-10 matrix is semantically incomplete for SK10 because it lists audit outputs but none of the frozen source, manifest, diff, closure, rule, or reviewer evidence inputs required to derive them.
concerns.evidence: The scope interpretation's D03 is distinct from, but linked to, the receipt-schema defect. Repairing receipt fields alone does not state which stage may inspect which source evidence, while adding visibility names alone would not make the receipt source-bound. SK10_EXTERNAL_SCOPE_AUDITOR sees authority and contract constants plus audit.change_sha256, tracked_files, observed_imports, forbidden_matches, cli_entrypoints, passed, and reviewer_interpretation_sha256. The declared information universe omits the audited repository root and frozen implementation bytes or manifest, per-file digests, repository diff and base, dependency/import and CLI discovery inputs, forbidden-match grammar, audit algorithm/version, reviewer identity/freshness evidence, and the referenced reviewer artifact itself. HUMAN_GOVERNANCE_REVIEW likewise has no direct view of that subject evidence. The matrix is therefore only syntactically complete over an incomplete universe. These inputs may live in a separately bound external-audit visibility artifact, but they must be visible only to SK10 and human review, forbidden to all runtime nodes, and permanently barred from scientific ingress.

concerns.statement: The visibility matrix names authority.human_ratification.change_sha256 as a direct field even though the bound ratification schema and validator expose no such property.
concerns.evidence: architecture_human_ratification.schema.json requires consensus_sha256 and human_required_state_sha256, and additionalProperties=false forbids change_sha256. architecture_intake validates consensus against the exact change and binds ratification to the exact consensus and paused state, so exact change provenance is transitively preserved; this is not an authority bypass. It is nevertheless a literal field-level contract mismatch: the authority stage cannot read the named ratification property from a valid artifact, and v4 does not say that the information item is a derived conceptual alias for consensus.architecture_change_sha256. Consensus must choose and bind one realizable reading—rename the cell to the actual transitive chain or add a direct field in newly hashed schema/validator bytes—without inferring that a nonexistent property was supplied.

concerns.statement: SK01-SK05 do not explicitly bind how the descriptor-to-role bijection renders role recipes into descriptor-space GRAPH, and their aggregate golden fields cannot detect the wrong convention.
concerns.evidence: The science interpretation had to assume that descriptor-space recipe triples use the inverse of pi. That is the natural type-correct reading, but the bound v3 consensus explicitly required revised bytes to bind inverse rendering and SK01's disposition requested fixed low-index vectors. V4 states only that pi is descriptor-to-role and GRAPH is in descriptor space; it never gives GRAPH(pi) as applying pi inverse to every role in each recipe, nor does it bind any indexed alignment, GRAPH, CAL, TOP, support-table, or chosen-pair vector. Treating the same raw permutation tuple as role-to-descriptor can permute per-index witnesses while preserving the 96/48/6 cardinalities, 1/4 and 1 values, twin aggregate failures, and the fixed golden report. A test deriving its expected graph and tie-break witnesses with the same mistaken helper can therefore pass. Exact inverse formulas and independently fixed vectors are pre-implementation oracle terms, not an implementation detail.

concerns.statement: SK08 closes the positive finite domains but not the negative test population, so its zero malformed-or-incompatible acceptance failures does not prove DomainError-before-computation for the advertised boundary.
concerns.evidence: The positive counts 12/96/27,648/192 and common-witness MOTIF compatibility are clear improvements. But the setup says malformed, noncanonical, and incompatible calls without a canonical malformed grammar, finite fixture registry, mutation construction, call count, expected exception surface, or receipt field for attempted negative cases. The result receipt [12,96,27648,192,0] is identical whether thousands of bound negative calls were rejected or none were attempted. The unbounded phrase every out-of-domain call is a function contract, not an executable exhaustive population over arbitrary Python values. This leaves the bound v3 requirement for canonical constructors, structural equality, and a closed externally callable malformed-input boundary only partially repaired. A nonempty deterministic negative registry or a constructor-only inaccessible boundary plus exact boundary tests must be fixed before implementation.
